about.title: About BISense
about.lead: An evidence-first research assistant for Indian Standards and BIS services, built for Smart India Hackathon 2026 (problem statement SIH26107).
about.problem: Manufacturers, MSMEs, students and consumers struggle to find which Indian Standards apply to a product, what those standards require, and how BIS certification, hallmarking and testing work. The answers are spread across thousands of documents, portals and PDFs. A general chatbot can sound confident while inventing clause numbers and limits. BISense instead answers only from an indexed library and shows exactly where each statement comes from.
about.how1: Documents are parsed into clauses with page numbers; tables are kept; watermarks and page furniture are removed.
about.how2: Each question is searched two ways (exact words with BM25, and meaning with local embeddings), and the results are combined and reranked.
about.how3: If nothing relevant is found, BISense says so without calling any AI model.
about.how4: The AI may only use the retrieved passages. A deterministic validator then checks every citation, quote, number, standard number and clause reference against the sources and removes anything unsupported.
about.how5: Hindi and Kannada questions are searched in English and answers are translated back with numbers, units and standard numbers protected.
about.evalMissing: No evaluation has been run on this machine yet. Run: npm run eval
about.evalNote: Numbers come from server/eval/questions.yaml run through the live pipeline; see docs/EVAL.md for the method and per-question results.
about.dataIntro: Every indexed file has a provenance record (source URL and retrieval date). Tiers:
about.tierA: Real Indian Standards obtained through official BIS channels and placed in data/raw by the team.
about.tierB: Public official pages and orders from bis.gov.in, fetched politely from an allow-list with their URL and date recorded.
about.tierC: Four short illustrative documents written for this prototype so every feature can be demonstrated. Their identifiers start with DEMO- and they are labelled everywhere.
about.limit1: The library is small and not exhaustive; an answer never implies that no other standard applies.
about.limit2: Full texts of Indian Standards are not bundled: they must be obtained through official BIS channels and ingested locally.
about.limit3: Scanned PDFs need OCR (Tesseract), which is optional; pages without text are reported, not indexed.
about.limit4: AI interpretations can be wrong; they are labelled and always point to the clause they explain.
about.limit5: Hindi and Kannada interface text was drafted by the team and needs native-speaker review.
about.limit6: Certification status comes only from the official BIS lists indexed on the retrieval date; it can change.
